kind: own R&D question set, regenerated from this system's records
data: This system's own ledgers: closed pull requests read from GitHub, the deploy record, the criticality ticks, the ultrastability ledger and the loop registry
title: Can an AI system close its own loops?
paper_title: Closing its own loops: what an AI system that runs itself shows about the human in every step
paper_frame: We state the common belief as properties that can fail, and test each against the records of a system that merges, deploys and checks its own work. Where it still depends on outside sessions, the paper says so with the number.
summary: A common belief holds that AI agents can draft code but a person must still merge it, deploy it and check that it works. Ultrastable is built to close those loops itself: a server-side lane merges green changes, every deploy is proven live against its commit, and every loop names its closing probe.

misperception.belief: AI agents can draft code, but a person still has to merge it, deploy it and check that it works.
misperception.short: A person must merge, deploy and check AI work.
misperception.counter: Merging, deploying and checking are loops, and loops can be closed by code: checks that can fail, a lane that merges what passes, a probe that proves the deploy live, and a revert when it is not.

findings.concern: Every loop says how it closes
findings.claim: Belief: an automated process needs a person to notice when it is done. Test: every registered loop declares a closing probe and a server-side owner.

mechanisms.how: a loop with no server-side owner fails the build
each loop row carries its trigger, closing probe and owner

findings.claim: Belief: a change waits for a person to merge it. Test: median hours from a pull request opening to its merge.

mechanisms.how: the server-side sweeper merges a green pull request
the lane reconciles conflicts with main and retries

findings.concern: Deploys are checked by the system
findings.claim: Belief: someone has to check that a deploy really worked. Test: share of uploaded deploys proven live against their own commit.

mechanisms.how: every deploy is read back and compared with its commit before it counts

findings.claim: Belief: automation still needs a hand on the wheel. Test: human touches counted by the latest criticality tick.

mechanisms.how: human touches are counted in the denominator of the system's own score

findings.concern: The system starts its own work
findings.claim: Belief: an AI system only does what a person asks. Test: share of merged pull requests the system's own loops opened.

mechanisms.how: the executor takes items from the queue in driver order and opens its own pull requests

findings.concern: The system ships its own deploys
findings.claim: Belief: shipping to production needs a person. Test: verified deploys the system originated and executed itself.

mechanisms.how: the tick wakes the executor, whose merged change deploys from the merge commit
